title: Fetter lane
html_source:
In chapter 9, Stephen’s thoughts go as follows:

Do and do. Thing done. In a rosery of Fetter Lane of Gerard, herbalist, he walks, greyedauburn. […] One life is all. One body. Do. But do.

The astute reader and Joyce are aware of the coming together of Stephen’s and Leopold’s minds. The astute reader is very aware of the writer at this point – a technique which occurs in other chapters (Paul Franssen, A. J. Hoenselaars. The Author as Character: Representing Historical Writers in Western Literature, p176).
